title: Happy Number
summary: Repeatedly replace a number by the sum of the squares of its digits and decide whether it reaches 1 or loops forever.

tests.explain: 4 → 16 → 37 → 58 → 89 → 145 → 42 → 20 → 4: the sequence loops without ever reaching 1.

hints: Write out the sequence for a few numbers. Either it reaches 1 (and stays there), or it repeats a number it has seen before. Why can't it grow forever?
A repeated number means the sequence is stuck in a loop. That's cycle detection on a linked list, where next(x) is the digit-square sum of x.
Run a slow pointer (one step) and a fast pointer (two steps) along the sequence until they meet. The number is happy exactly when they meet at 1.

complexity.time: O(log n): the first step shrinks any big number to a few hundred, and the walk from there is short
complexity.space: O(1) with fast and slow pointers (a Set of seen numbers also works)
